title: Recording: Everybody Wins by Ringo Starr | 1991
content:
Conway Recording Studios, Los Angeles
Producer: Peter Asher
Engineer: Frank Wolf

Ringo Starr recorded ‘Everybody Wins’ for his tenth solo album, Time Takes Time, on 10 September 1991.

It was co-written by Starr and Johnny Warman, an English singer-songwriter best known for his 1981 album Walking Into Mirrors. In the 1970s Warman had been signed to Starr’s Ring O’Records as a songwriter on a one-year retainer.

Warman wrote ‘Don’t Go Where The Road Don’t Go’, ‘After All These Years’, ‘Runaways’, and ‘Everybody Wins’ with Starr for Time Takes Time. He also supported the All-Starr Band in London, and ‘Don’t Go Where The Road Don’t Go’ became part of the band’s live setlist.

‘Everybody Wins’ was recorded by Starr on 10, 11, 12, and 18 September 1991. It was released on the ‘Don’t Go Where The Road Don’t Go’ CD single in September the following year.

The story on that is so strange, because I wrote it with Johnny Warman in 1992. We did a track with Peter Asher on it, and it didn’t make it to the album; the arrangement was just too long, there were too many big gaps. It didn’t work, and sometimes it doesn’t.

So I looked at it again, but I didn’t have a copy. Peter Asher didn’t have a copy. We had to go on the internet, find it – somebody had it – and we had to put a mic in front of the computer to get a copy! It my song – you can’t get me, and I’m on it! But no-one had a copy. I couldn’t find it. This is the way of the world, to find your own gear, ’cause over the years you’ve put it somewhere.

Ringo Starr

Starr re-recorded the song for 2010’s Y Not, retitling it ‘Everyone Wins’. The new recording featured Starr’s brother-in-law Joe Walsh on guitar.
